leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part prize for B031 (GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapies) with the same laureates, Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and citations that differ only in wording. Shared reasoning: originality, mechanistic clarity, independently confirmed outcome trials, and breadth across diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. Not shared: the weight given to drug development. Several members frame the citation around hormone discovery and physiology, while Wahren-Herlenius asks that the citation also name the therapies that followed so that excluding Knudsen is not read as a verdict on the drugs. Wahren-Herlenius, who ranked B046 first in the opening and had proposed Knudsen instead of Mojsov, moved to the trio in round 1. Five members' statements explicitly say that the count of first-place rankings is not merit in itself.

areas_of_agreement: All six members prefer B031 as a single-achievement prize with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov in round 1.
All six name attribution, specifically the Mojsov versus Habener priority question and the exclusion of Knudsen, as the main weakness of B031 and not its scientific merit.
All six say they weigh B031 on the evidence (originality, maturity, breadth) and not on the number of first-place rankings.
Members converge on treating optogenetics (B019) as a tool whose six-name credit cannot fit three places, and on treating CAR-T (B016) as a strong clinical case with an attribution gap around Eshhar.

Four members (Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius) describe the unfolded protein response (B042), TNF blockade (B046) or imatinib (B012) as sound candidates but not ahead of B031 this year. Svenningsson-Per likewise places B046 in a later year, and El-Manira treats B042 as a later-year prize.
Several members note that a second part would force a cut within the GLP-1 trio because of the three-person cap, and none proposes a two-part configuration in round 1.
scientific_disputes: Whether optogenetics (B019) is a discovery about a light-gated channel (Perlmann, Svenningsson-Per) or primarily a tool rather than a disease mechanism (El-Manira, Sandberg, Svenningsson-Per, Wahren-Herlenius); clinical translation is described as early.

Whether the unfolded protein response (B042) is conceptually original and mature (Linnarsson) or too indirect in medical consequence, with mammalian PERK and ATF6 branches outside the credit (El-Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson-Per, Wahren-Herlenius).

How much weight demonstrated effect on human disease should carry relative to methodological breadth; Wahren-Herlenius states she weights demonstrated clinical effect more heavily than El-Manira's framing of optogenetics suggests.
How to describe the GLP-1 achievement in the citation given that long-term safety, durability of weight loss and newer indications are still being characterised.
attribution_disputes: B031 third slot: Mojsov (discovery-level identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide) versus Knudsen (long-acting analogue design). Five members prefer Mojsov in round 1. Wahren-Herlenius, the one member whose opening proposal named Knudsen, now accepts the trio but asks that the claim be scrutinised.

Mojsov's priority relative to the Habener group, who are not among the credited names, is flagged as unsettled by all six; Svenningsson-Per, Wahren-Herlenius and others say the historical record is being relied on from memory and is not verified from the supplied evidence.

B019 optogenetics: six credited names for three places. Three members propose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel, and Linnarsson proposes Deisseroth, Hegemann and Miesenböck. Any trio omits at least three credible names (Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck or Nagel).

B016 CAR-T: Eshhar's chimeric-receptor concept lies outside the credited names. Svenningsson-Per questions Rosenberg's link to CAR-specific engineering, and Wahren-Herlenius proposed only June and Sadelain in her opening.

B046, B012, B033, B037, B042: members cite contributors outside the credited names (for example Cerami, Vilcek and Kollias for TNF; Rowley and Witte for BCR-ABL; Ron and Kaufman for the UPR; Sabatini and Heitman for TOR).
maturity_disputes: Whether GLP-1 recognition is timely and arguably overdue after decades of evidence (stated by El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Svenningsson-Per, Wahren-Herlenius) with only the long-term safety and obesity data still accumulating.
Whether imatinib (B012) is late and already widely recognised, including by Lasker awards (Sandberg), which weakens the sense of an unrecognised achievement.

Whether optogenetics, the unfolded protein response and TNF blockade are better held for a later year because clinical translation is early (B019, B042) or because the field has had decades to reward the work (B046, per Svenningsson-Per).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member reports a recusal issue for any shortlisted ballot.

Svenningsson-Per (chair) declares about twenty co-authored works with committee member Perlmann on subjects unrelated to the shortlist, and a postdoctoral link to Greengard, which is also unrelated to the shortlist; he also notes neuroscience colleagues in the optogenetics field are close to his area.

El-Manira declares a 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann (not about a shortlisted discovery), co-authorships with Grillner and Ernfors on other topics, and familiarity with optogenetics as a tool in motor-circuit work.
Sandberg declares co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisén, none involving shortlisted work.
Wahren-Herlenius works in autoimmunity and rheumatology, close to B046, but documents no tie to Feldmann, Maini or other shortlisted candidates.
Linnarsson and Perlmann report no specific conflict; both note documented connections do not involve shortlisted names.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee settle, from the supplied evidence and without relying on recollection, whether Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is sufficient for a laureate slot given the Habener group's claim, and if it cannot, what the name list becomes?

Should the third B031 slot go to discovery of the active peptide (Mojsov) or to development of long-acting analogues (Knudsen), and how should the citation be worded so that either choice does not read as a verdict on the other contribution?

Is a single-achievement GLP-1 prize preferred over a two-part prize, given that any second achievement would force a cut within the three-person cap, and if a second part is wanted, which candidate (B016, B042, B046, B019) and which names?
For B019, does the six-name credit make optogenetics unsuitable this year regardless of merit, and if the committee proceeds, what principle chooses the three laureates?
For B016, how should Eshhar's absence from the credited names and the link between Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and CAR engineering be handled in any trio?
Does any member see a concrete clinical anchor for the unfolded protein response (B042) that would move it ahead of its current position as a later-year candidate?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows unusually broad convergence: all six configurations are the same B031 trio, and the open issues are attribution and citation framing, not scientific merit. The convergence follows independent opening rankings, and members state that it does not itself count as merit. Round 2 should therefore test the Mojsov and Knudsen choice and the unverified priority record before any vote, and should treat the alternatives (B016, B019, B046, B042) as separate cases with their own attribution gaps.
